newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast crudes seen undercut by LATAM crudes.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast crudes seen undercut by LATAM crudes.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude markets were idle Monday, with all types of South American volumes undercutting local grades, traders said.
A trading house continued to offer South Blend cargo (29 API, 0.8 sulphur) to West Coast (PADD 5) refiners at a price rumored to be 60 to 80 cents a gallon under ANS.
"That's a hell of a deal. That's going to put a lot of pressure on (ANS) crude," one buyer said.
The grade does not require as much desulphurization as ANS, according to some buyers, and makes it more economical to process into light products.

Two major producers and one refinery offered large parcels of Line 63 light, a blended crude similar to ANS. They asked for 70 cents over Buena Vista grade crude, 30 cents under the last reported deal.
Two were sized at 4,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) for May, and a third for 5,000 bpd.
On a notional basis, Line 63 was talked $2.37/2.27 under May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI). The grade rarely trades off WTI.
BP Oil, the dominant seller of ANS, last offered at 95 cents below May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI).
In heavy crude markets, all California lowered prices for Point Arguella offshore crude by 0.50 cents a barrel as of April 17.
With more Venezuelan and Mexican heavy grades moving into the U.S. Gulf, shipments of Point Arguello east have been discounted into the West Coast.
West Coast benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) last traded a week ago at $1.32 below West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI), which compared with a week earlier at $1.05 below.
Outright ANS prices rose 50 cents a barrel, in line with a technical rise in West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude Monday.
